# Visual and Animation Production Pipeline

**D:** Stylized 3D with Babylon.js; editable Blender sources and glTF/GLB delivery; one base and one upgrade per creature.  
**P:** This production method, visual direction, budgets and acceptance gates. No models, textures, animation clips, music or runtime code are generated by this document.

## 1. Visual goal

Aim for a readable mythological miniature world: strong silhouettes, expressive creatures, sculpted terrain, warm stone and bronze, purposeful cloth accents, and atmospheric lighting. Detail should reward the unit viewer without making battle stacks difficult to distinguish at gameplay zoom. Preserve the parchment/stone/navy/gold direction of the early boards as a proposed interface palette, not a requirement to copy their ornament or illegible text.

The initial Greek kit should look like one art direction across humans, monsters, buildings, props, portraits and UI. The game is inspired by mythological strategy, not a reproduction of Heroes III or Age of Mythology assets. Do not extract their models, textures, music, animations, icons or biographies. Record provenance and permission for every external asset used.

## 2. What generation means

Image generation may help produce reference concepts, mood studies, character turnarounds and texture ideas. An attractive image is **not** a rigged 3D creature, a usable topology, a valid animation clip, an orthographically consistent model sheet or a collision footprint. Text-to-3D or stock assets, if used, still pass the same cleanup, retopology, rigging, licensing and runtime checks.

Choose one approved design per family before making its many derivatives. Do not independently generate sixteen unrelated creature images and ask the developer to turn them into a coherent army. Prefer a reusable base sculpture and rig, with explicit upgrade additions. AI-assisted authoring is optional; the final runtime never calls a generation service.

## 3. Asset packet required before authoring

Every asset gets an ID, role, screen usage, scale reference, base/upgrade relationship if applicable, required views, materials, sockets, animation states, collision/footprint policy, budget, accessible description and source/provenance record. Creature packets are in the [paired creature bible](03_creature_pairs_and_animation_bible.md). Non-creature coverage is in the [element inventory](04_environment_towns_ui_and_audio.md).

Create a neutral reference scene containing a 1.8-meter human, one/two-hex footprint guides, a flat test light, the battlefield camera and the bestiary camera. Check silhouette and proportions in this scene before spending time on surface detail. This is a presentation reference, not a change to logical unit scale or reach.

## 4. End-to-end creature workflow

### Gate A - Design the pair

Produce a shared front, side, back and three-quarter sheet at the same scale, first in grayscale silhouette, then in material blocks. Lock anatomy and equipment placement across views. Add a labeled upgrade-delta panel rather than redesigning the species. The upgrade must read through at least one silhouette/equipment difference and one material/detail difference; color alone is not sufficient.

Approve the pair in a small battlefield montage as well as close-up. If the Hoplite's upgrade looks like a different faction or the Griffin's plume obscures its count label, revise now. Preserve a source-status note separating historical/mythological inspiration from original game design.

### Gate B - Model and prepare topology

Block out in Blender, compare to the shared scale guides, then create a clean deformation mesh. An AI/stock mesh may be a starting point; repair intersecting limbs, fused equipment, hidden internal faces, non-manifold pieces, asymmetry errors, and implausible joints. Remove geometry never visible at either gameplay or codex distance.

Create separate logical objects for body, equipment and optional upgrade attachments where practical. Weapons/armor remain attached to named bones or sockets, not independent physics entities. Avoid excessive separate draw calls. Establish a low-poly runtime mesh before baking details from any high-resolution source.

### Gate C - UVs and materials

Use a consistent texel density and material vocabulary. Base color and emissive textures use color interpretation; normal and packed occlusion/roughness/metallic data use linear interpretation. Proposed ORM packing is R=occlusion, G=roughness, B=metallic. Check actual exported materials, not just the Blender viewport.

Prefer one body material and one equipment material for ordinary units. Keep feather/cloth alpha coverage controlled; avoid many intersecting transparent layers. Team identity is a separate mask/accent or banner and must not overwrite the family or upgrade identity. Give both forms their own portraits even when they share most texture data.

### Gate D - Rig once, support both forms

Create a reusable deform skeleton for each anatomical family. Base and upgrade share bone names, bind pose, orientation, skinning convention and socket IDs. Upgraded equipment is weighted or attached to that same skeleton. Human rigs can share source motion after a checked retarget; a Griffin or Centaur is not a stretched humanoid rig.

Proposed sockets: `socket_weapon_r`, `socket_weapon_l`, `socket_projectile`, `socket_fx`, `socket_label`. A manifest records only sockets actually used. Do not add a projectile socket to a melee-only creature to imply a new ability. The label position may be a presentation offset rather than a deform bone.

Control rigs and constraints remain editable in `.blend`. Export baked deform motion and test it in Babylon; do not assume the runtime executes Blender IK, cloth simulation or arbitrary shader nodes. Blender's documented export modes differ by release, including action/NLA handling, so pin the exporter preset and verify the actual clip list [T02](../reference/05_production_sources.md).

### Gate E - Animate and test mechanics alignment

Author in-place locomotion. The presentation system moves the model along a prevalidated path; it does not derive movement distance from root drift. Attacks have anticipation, contact/release and recovery, but do not include rule effects not present in the unit definition. A magical-looking Temple Adept bolt remains that unit's ordinary ranged attack, not a second mana spell.

Proposed source sampling is 30 FPS, exported as time-based animation and resampled as needed. Idle 2-4 seconds, locomotion 0.7-1.3 seconds per cycle, melee/shoot 0.8-1.4 seconds, hit 0.2-0.45 seconds, defeat 1-1.8 seconds, victory 1.5-2.5 seconds. These are art-timing targets, not combat durations or simulator ticks.

Test contacts, foot sliding, hand grip, wing clearance, lance/armor clipping, balance, and base/upgrade motion reuse. Poses at the ends of a loop must match. Defeat is a non-looping state; it never defaults to autoplay in the bestiary. A guard pose must remain distinguishable from attack anticipation.

### Gate F - Export and validate

Use glTF 2.0 / GLB. Keep `.blend`, textures and source rigs separately; glTF is a runtime delivery format rather than a full editable authoring archive [T03](../reference/05_production_sources.md). Export one file per form initially, with shared source animation data allowed. Explicit LOD files may be selected through our manifest; no engine-specific LOD extension is mandatory.

Run the Khronos glTF Validator and keep its report. It validates format, references, buffers and animation structure, but does not establish good skin deformation or art quality [T12](../reference/05_production_sources.md). Also inspect every required clip in Babylon under the production light, graphics backend and shader/material setup.

### Gate G - Integrate all game contexts

Bind the runtime asset to its existing creature ID, not its display name. Generate the portrait and army icon from the approved 3D model in a shared camera/light setup. Verify battle, map marker, recruitment, hero army, comparison, and full bestiary usage. Confirm the upgraded unit has the right ID, footage, statistics and rank badge in each context.

Test missing texture, missing optional clip, interrupted load, fast scene switching and reduced motion. A required asset missing in a production build fails content validation. A development fallback remains usable and explicitly marked, not silently presented as finished art.

## 5. Coordinates, origin and scale

Runtime assets use meters, Y-up and a right-handed scene. The glTF specification defines +Z as the front direction [T03](../reference/05_production_sources.md). Set Babylon's right-handed scene policy before loading [T01](../reference/05_production_sources.md). Author Blender models Z-up and facing -Y under the tested glTF conversion preset; verify a forward-arrow calibration asset rather than applying a guessed second rotation.

Apply intended scale/rotation before binding the deform skeleton. Do not apply arbitrary transform resets to an already animated rig without rebaking. Avoid negative-scale mirroring. The root is at the feet/ground projection for a standing form; a flying form retains the same ground anchor and uses presentation altitude above it.

The logical footprint belongs to the rules: one or two cells. A `visualOffset` can center a two-cell model over its actual footprint, but it must not move its hit-test target or enlarge melee range. Huge wings may overhang graphically; unit selection and legal landing still use the explicit occupied cells.

## 6. Starting budgets to measure

| Asset class | Proposed LOD0 triangle range | Other starting limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Human infantry/caster | 6,000-12,000 | 1-2 materials, up to 64 deform bones, mostly 2K texture sets |
| Cavalry/Centaur | 16,000-28,000 | Up to 96 deform bones for the combined rider/horse rig |
| Griffin | 18,000-30,000 | Up to 96 deform bones; feather overdraw reviewed |
| Minotaur/Cyclops | 12,000-24,000 | Strong silhouette, limited accessories/materials |
| Repeated terrain prop | 100-2,000 | Shared atlases/materials and instancing where suitable |
| Landmark/town focal building | 8,000-25,000 | LOD/chunk visibility; no interior unless visible |

Begin LOD1 around 50% and LOD2 around 20% of LOD0, preserving silhouette, sockets and rig compatibility. These are not universal limits or measured results. Texture memory, skinning, shadow passes, particles, draw calls and transparent overdraw all matter; triangle count alone is not the budget.

Represent each stack with a bounded formation: proposed three visible small soldiers, two medium beasts/mounted units, or one apex creature. Counts remain exact in labels. Low quality may show one actor per stack. Fifty Hoplites never require fifty independently simulated characters. Phase-offset cosmetic idles use a separate presentation seed.

Cache shared geometry/materials and pool transient projectiles/effects. Independent skinned animations need appropriately separated skeleton state; do not assume ordinary static instancing automatically supplies independently animated rigs. Measure the complete fourteen-stack battlefield and repeated bestiary visits.

## 7. Animation manifest contract

A form manifest references model paths, LODs, portrait, sockets, clip aliases, loops and optional normalized presentation cue points. Values below are an example shape, not a claim that the asset exists.

```json
{
  "assetId": "unit.griffin.base",
  "creatureId": "griffin",
  "familyId": "griffin",
  "form": "base",
  "status": "planned",
  "model": "units/greek/griffin/base/model.glb",
  "portrait": "units/greek/griffin/base/portrait.webp",
  "rigId": "rig.griffin.v1",
  "clips": {
    "idle": {"name": "idle_a", "loop": true},
    "fly": {"name": "move_fly", "loop": true},
    "melee": {"name": "attack_melee_a", "loop": false, "impactAt": 0.52},
    "hit": {"name": "hit_a", "loop": false},
    "defeat": {"name": "defeat", "loop": false},
    "victory": {"name": "victory", "loop": false}
  },
  "visualOffset": [0, 0, 0],
  "provenanceId": "provenance.griffin.v1"
}
```

Required clip sets are family-specific; this short example omits the full production list. Animation import must not auto-play a random first clip. A runtime binding validates every mapped name, duration and loop policy before enabling its viewer selector.

## 8. Runtime playback state machine

An idle actor can enter a queued move, turn, melee, shoot, ability, hit, guard, defeat or victory presentation. Transitions are driven by immutable rules events. Retaliation is a separate response event, not automatically triggered by the visible hit animation. Projectiles are cosmetic and use the resolved target; a physics miss cannot undo resolved damage.

Cue points synchronize sound/flash with the known result. Use event ID deduplication so skipping an attack does not play its impact again later. Interrupting/cancelling playback snaps the presentation to the current authoritative state. Defeated actors cannot keep receiving queued attacks; dispose or cancel stale events by revision and actor ID.

Settings: 1x, 2x and Instant combat; manual bestiary playback at 0.5x/1x/2x; Pause/Stop/Restart; optional orbit for actual 3D assets; no forced camera shake. Reduced motion disables idle autoplay, camera sway, pulsing backgrounds and automatic spinning. An explicit user-requested clip can play once with an immediate Stop control. The prior [behavior contract](../content/02_animation_behavior_contract.md) remains the interaction baseline.

## 9. File organization and review status

```text
assets-src/units/greek/griffin/
  design/                  # shared pair sheet, silhouette and material references
  griffin_family.blend     # editable base, upgrade attachments, rig and actions
  textures/                # layered/source textures and baked maps
  review/                  # turntables, contact sheets, provenance and QA
assets-runtime/units/greek/griffin/
  base/model.glb
  base/portrait.webp
  upgraded/model.glb
  upgraded/portrait.webp
  family.manifest.json
```

Use asset states `briefed -> concept_approved -> modeled -> rigged -> animated -> exported -> integrated -> verified`. A file's existence is not verification. Store creator/source/license, exporter version, content version, hashes and review owner. Never place license keys, service credentials, or personal source material in a public asset packet.

## 10. Practical production order

Finish the Hoplite pair end to end first; then Peltast, Cavalry and Griffin pairs to prove humanoid, ranged, mounted and flight pipelines. Complete Temple Adept/Seer, Centaur/Sentinel, Minotaur/Warden, and Cyclops/Stormforged after those pipelines work. Build town/environment kits and UI in parallel from their own briefs, not by inventing new unit definitions.

A polished complete pair is more informative than sixteen disconnected renders. The campaign release still requires the complete pairs for every family it contains. Do not commission only the base units and treat upgrades as a last-minute color filter.
